question: Will the UK increase the qualifying period for settlement to 10 years before May 2026?

forecasts.reference-class: Earned settlement policy reform establishing a 10-year baseline qualifying period for settlement (ILR) with potential reductions or extensions based on contributions and other factors

sources.claim: The government proposes increasing the default qualifying period for settlement to 10 years under an earned settlement framework, with a time-adjustment model across four pillars (Character, Integration, Contribution, Residence).

House of Commons Library notes that the government announced details in November 2025; a baseline 10-year period is proposed for many migrants, with some groups qualifying sooner or later based on circumstances.

Migration Observatory explains the consultation is open until February 12, 2026, and that most migrants would face longer or equal waiting periods under the new rules; high earners may access faster paths in some cases.
KPMG outlines the proposed 10-year standard and longer timelines (up to 15, 20, or 30 years) under the earned settlement framework depending on category and circumstances.
Official changes to immigration rules reflect ongoing reform of settlement-related requirements and resemble a shift toward longer residence-based pathways.
IPPR analysis cited by The Guardian suggests hundreds of thousands of children could face a 10-year wait for settled status under the proposed reforms.

The default baseline qualifying period for settlement would increase to 10 years under the earned settlement framework; the document outlines 10-year baseline and four pillars (Character, Integration, Contribution, Residence) used to determine eligibility.
On November 20, 2025, the UK government launched an open consultation on earned settlement, proposing to raise the standard qualifying period for settlement from five to 10 years.
Migration Observatory explains that the default 10-year baseline is under consultation, with longer waiting periods for many migrants; the public consultation closes on 12 February 2026.
The Guardian reports that the government proposed to extend the waiting period for permanent settlement from five to ten years as part of immigration policy plans.
IPPR analysis cited in the Guardian suggests changes could significantly affect hundreds of thousands of children in the settlement pathway.
The government announced a major overhaul of legal migration, doubling the permanent settlement qualifying period to 10 years with transitional arrangements.
The Commons Library notes the baseline 10-year qualifying period has been announced, with exemptions and a phased rollout.
